sections.h2: What makes a Willingboro sale different from a typical New Jersey sale?
sections.html:
Willingboro makes the seller clear a township certificate of occupancy before ownership changes, and the inspection must be booked a full 15 days ahead of settlement. That clock drives the rest of the sale: heating certification, any repairs, a possible reinspection and then the filing in Mount Holly.

Willingboro is a Burlington County suburb of Philadelphia, home to 32,824 people. The sections below cover local numbers, resale rules, tax steps and the trade-offs between an agent, a sale on your own and a cash buyer.

sections.h2: What do the Willingboro numbers say about homes and households?
sections.html:
Willingboro grew from a single builder's plan, and the figures still reflect it. Owners live in 84.3 percent of homes, households average 3.02 people, and 7.73 square miles of land hold about 4,128 people per square mile. The 2020 count was 31,889, and the mid-2025 estimate reads 32,824.

sections.h2: What is the Levittown story behind Willingboro's neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Willingboro began as the Constabulary of Wellingborrow on November 6, 1688, and the legislature made it a township on February 21, 1798. Its present shape comes from the 1950s and 1960s, when Levitt and Sons built its third and largest Levittown here. The first homes sold in June 1958, and the population climbed from 852 in 1950 to 43,386 in 1970.

Residents voted in 1959 to call it Levittown Township, and a second referendum in November 1963 brought the old name back. The planning left a pattern buyers still use to find a house:

  • Neighborhoods are called parks, such as Pennypacker Park, Millbrook Park, Windsor Park and Hawthorne Park.
  • Streets inside each park start with the same letter as the park's name, so a Pennypacker address starts with P.
  • Country Club Ridge was planned around a golf course in the 1960s.
  • Pennypacker Park and Country Club Park hold the community pools.

Many houses here came from a small set of Levitt floor plans, so a buyer can often compare yours with the same model a few streets away. Mention additions and the age of the roof and furnace when you present the house.

sections.h2: How do Route 130, the bus lines and the schools figure in?
sections.html:
U.S. Route 130 marks the northwest boundary, while Rancocas Creek drains the southwest side. Willingboro borders Burlington Township, Delanco, Delran, Edgewater Park, Moorestown, Mount Laurel and Westampton. Of its 122.11 miles of roads, 109.02 miles are township-maintained.

Transit is by bus. NJ Transit routes 409, 417 and 418 run between Trenton and Philadelphia, BurLink runs two local routes, and Academy Bus links Willingboro to Midtown and Lower Manhattan.

The district, Willingboro Township Public Schools, ran nine schools with 3,456 students in 2020-21. Hawthorne, W.R. James Sr. and Twin Hills serve grades 1 to 4, Levitt Intermediate covers grades 5 and 6, Memorial Middle School covers 7 and 8, and Willingboro High School covers 9 to 12. Families will ask which school serves your park, so find out before the first showing.

sections.h2: How does the Willingboro certificate of occupancy process work?
sections.html:
Chapter 199 of the township code, the housing standards chapter, bars a change of ownership or occupancy until the Department of Inspections issues a certificate of occupancy. The ordinance sets these steps:

  • The owner or agent applies and pays the fee set in the township fee schedule.
  • The visit must be set no later than 15 calendar days ahead of settlement, and a request made within four days of it adds an $80 expedite charge.
  • Cancel or move the appointment with a day's notice, or the first fee is charged regardless.
  • The inspector makes a visual check of accessible parts of the structure, which is not a guarantee of electrical, plumbing or heating systems.
  • A qualified technician authorized by the township must separately certify the heating equipment, and that certification can be no more than 30 days old when the certificate issues.
  • If the house fails, the department sends a written list of defects, and the owner then has 30 days from the visit to repair them and ask for a recheck.

Ask the Department of Inspections for the current fee and application steps. If the buyer will take on repairs, say so in the contract so both sides know who pays.

sections.h2: Where does the Willingboro deed go, and what fees does the state add?
sections.html:
The Burlington County Clerk's main office, 50 Rancocas Road in Mount Holly, takes deeds on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. The clerk also runs a free Property Fraud Alert service that flags any paper filed under your name.

One paperwork rule changed recently. County staff reject any GIT/REP seller declaration signed on or after October 1, 2025 that is not on the latest state form.

For prices up to $350,000 the state's realty transfer fee runs $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, then $3.35 per $500 through $200,000, then $3.90 per $500 through $350,000. At a $270,300 price, those three tiers total roughly $1,480, a number your closing agent will confirm.

sections.h2: What are Willingboro's tax dates and the October tax sale?
sections.html:
Bills follow the calendar year, with installments due on the first of February, May, August and November and a ten-day grace period after each. From the eleventh day, interest is figured back to the first, and a postmark earns no credit.

Payments go to the window in the municipal building, the Police Department drop box, the mail or the township's online portal. The tax office sits in Suite 205 at One Rev. Dr. M. L. King Jr. Drive, with window hours from 9 in the morning to 4:30. The portal rejects prior-year balances, so get an exact payoff figure from the collector before closing.

A balance left open past December 31 enters the township's electronic tax sale, held every October for earlier unpaid taxes and municipal charges. The 2026 auction was set for October 14. Senior, veteran and disabled-person deductions are handled by the assessor's office at 609-877-2200.

sections.h2: Which fits a Willingboro owner best: agent, own sale or cash buyer?
sections.html:
A listing can bring the strongest price for a clean house, a cash buyer removes the repair cycle, and selling alone falls between them. Timing is the real difference, because of the 15-day inspection lead.

  • An agent suits a house in good repair that can pass inspection without a long defect list.
  • A solo sale suits an owner who follows recent prices in the neighborhood and will hire an attorney for the contract.
  • A cash purchase suits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant or an estate, since the buyer can take over the defect list.

Book the township inspection the moment a closing date exists, and measure each offer by the cash that reaches you after transfer fee, taxes and payoff.

faqs.q: Is an inspection mandatory before a Willingboro sale?
faqs.a: Yes. A certificate of occupancy is needed before ownership changes, and the visit must be booked 15 calendar days ahead. A qualified technician must also certify the heating equipment.

faqs.q: What if the inspector finds defects?
faqs.a: The department issues a written notice of defects. You have 30 days from the inspection to finish repairs and request a reinspection, and the certificate follows once the house passes.

faqs.q: What are the Willingboro installment dates?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November, each followed by ten grace days. Postmarks are ignored, and balances still open after December 31 enter the October tax sale.

faqs.q: Which office records a Willingboro deed?
faqs.a: The Burlington County Clerk's main office, 50 Rancocas Road in Mount Holly, which serves the public on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

faqs.q: Can a Willingboro house with tenants or repair needs be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The certificate rules still apply, but an as-is buyer can agree to take over the defect list and the occupancy. Spell out who handles the inspection and repairs in the contract.
